newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Deutsche moves Belgian OLO trading to UK - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche moves Belgian OLO trading to UK - dealers.

text.p: The Brussels branch of Deutsche Bank AG, one of the 15 primary dealers of Belgian state debt, has moved most of its linear bond (OLO) trading activity from Brussels to London since the start of the year, Belgian OLO dealers said.
"Effectively, Deutsche is acting as a primary dealer from London," said one OLO dealer, who declined to be identified.

However London-based Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG), the investment banking arm of Deutsche Bank, denied that it was acting as a primary dealer from London and said that its London traders were only supporting the Brussels-based team.
"We still operate a primary dealership in Belgian bonds from Brussels, but with the support from London," a London-based DMG spokesman told Reuters.
The bank still had one OLO trader in Belgium, but often Belgian customers calling Deutsche Bank Brussels automatically got switched to the London office, dealers in other banks said.
"Deutsche has minimal staff in Brussels, and maximum in London," a source close to Deutsche Bank said.
Deutsche Bank Brussels, however, is still the official counter party in the deals, and also handles the back office and all the administration in Brussels, a DMG chief trader said.

Belgian dealers said the Belgian Treasury was annoyed with Deutsche Bank's de facto move, as it had several requests from foreign banks to become primary dealers in Belgian debt in the run up to a single currency in 1999.
"Deutsche Bank has set a precedent, which makes it politically much more difficult for the Treasury to say no to foreign applicants," one OLO dealer said.
A Treasury official said the Deutsche Bank situation was "a bit difficult", and confirmed that there had been foreign requests, but added that none had received a positive answer so far.
"A number of foreign banks have asked to become primary dealers in Belgian state debt, with some insistence. We are considering that possibility, but no decision has been made," the official said.
"Deutsche Bank still has a representation in Belgium, and they still have one trader here," the official added.

The primary dealer system, set up in 1991, requires primary dealers to continuously quote bid and ask prices in linear bonds. In exchange, they can participate in the Treasury's non-competitive OLO and Treasury bill auctions and enjoy a preferential relationship with the central bank.
